subject: Command for mirt with same 'grm' function for ltm

messages.author: 39cabec970606186
messages.subject: Command for mirt with same 'grm' function for ltm
parts:
I used in itm the following SAMEJIMA gradual commands
COMMANDS IN LTM
Mod2 <-grm (FATOR_ACEITACAO, constrained = TRUE, Hessian = TRUE) #Hessian estimate the EP

Mod1 <-grm (FATOR_ACEITACAO, Hessian = TRUE)

But when I used the 'graded' command on mirt:
mod4 <-mirt (FACTORY_ACEITACAO, 1, itemtype = 'graded')

the value of the coefficients of the same dataset was different, it made me think that there could be a specific command in mirt for the same analysis I did in ltm, so my question is for those commands 'gsm' SAMEJIMA (constant and variable) do itm, what would be the command in the MIRT .. if you can help me thank you.

NOTE: I also used the 'grsm' command and it did not work

coefientes itm:
      Extrmt1 Extrmt2 Extrmt3 Extrmt4 Dscrmn
CERQ_S1 -1.410 -0.142 0.653 1.578 2.18
CERQ_S5 -1.423 -0.301 0.490 1.248 2.18

MIRT Coefficients: (graded)
       a b1 b2 b3 b4
CERQ_S1 1,387 -1,755 -0,178 0.794 1,959
CERQ_S5 11,725 ​​-1,128 -0,245 0.384 0.978

                                   (grsm)
         a1 d1 d2 d3 d4 c
CERQ_S1 2.014 2.937 0.322 -1.413 -3.246 0.000
CERQ_S5 2,379 2,937 0.322 -1,413 -3,246 0.345

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Command for mirt with same 'grm' function for ltm
parts:
You are including a constrained = argument in ltm, which constrains all the slopes to be equal (the tell here is that both models with have different log-likelihood values). But you haven't done that in mirt, which would require passing some mirt.model() object with a CONSTRAIN argument. grsm is also a very different itemtype, and one that ltm cannot fit.   

Phil
